遍.meaning: A skater nails wheels to an old <part>notice board</part> and rides it down every <part>ramp</part> in the city, the flyers still pinned to it peeling off in the wind. By noon there are lost-parrot posters on rooftops, buses and one puzzled cow. They're <kanji>everywhere</kanji>.
遍.on: A <sound>hen</sound> pecks one off the pavement and wears it as a cape.
遍.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>!' gasps a <sound>ma</sound>ma on a balcony as a flyer flutters into her butterfly <sound>ne</sound>t.

唯.meaning: At a bird choir contest, a hundred beaks open wide, but the judges creep along the rows and find that only one <part>mouth</part> is making a sound: a tiny <part>sparrow</part> at the back. The rest were miming. She takes the trophy, won <kanji>solely</kanji> by her own song.
唯.on: Her prize is a <sound>yu</sound>zu, which she shares with an <sound>ee</sound>l in the pond.
唯.kun: The mimers sulk on top of a <sound>ta</sound>co stand, and a <sound>du</sound>ck tells them they only have themselves to blame.

郊.meaning: The last bus stop is marked by a single <part>pennant</part> on a pole. Here bankers stepping off the bus <part>mingle</part> with goats chewing the timetable, and a tractor waits at the zebra crossing. Not quite town, not quite country: the <kanji>outskirts</kanji>.
郊.on: A goat swipes a banker's ice cream <sound>co</sound>ne and trots off into the fields.

累.meaning: Each day a scarecrow in the <part>rice field</part> ties one knot in a long <part>thread</part> to count the crows he has scared off. The thread coils round his post, trails across the paddy and wraps the farmhouse twice. The knots never stop: they <kanji>accumulate</kanji>.
累.on: In the end the thread drags down an old stone <sound>ru</sound>in at the edge of the field.

貌.meaning: A <part>leopard</part> tired of its spots paints itself <part>white</part>, stands up on its back <part>legs</part> and strolls into town wearing a tie. Nobody knows it, and the shop windows show a stranger. Same cat inside, brand-new <kanji>form</kanji>.
貌.on: It hides behind a <sound>bou</sound>lder when a real leopard pads past.
貌.kun: '<sound>Ca</sound>lm down,' it tells a barking dog, and offers it a <sound>ta</sound>co and some <sound>chee</sound>se.

冠.meaning: The king has lost his headgear, so the palace carpenter makes do: a velvet <part>blanket</part> draped over a <part>sawhorse</part>, with a gold <part>golf club</part> stuck in the top as a spike. The king wears the lot to the ball, wooden legs past his ears. Wobbly, but it's a <kanji>crown</kanji>.
冠.on: The queen tucks a pink <sound>carn</sound>ation behind one wooden leg.
冠.kun: She pins on a <sound>carn</sound>ation, a <sound>moo</sound>se at the ball eats it, and the king hides behind a <sound>ree</sound>d fan.

紡.meaning: A sailor ties loose wool to the mast. When the wind fills the <part>sail</part>, the whole ship twirls in the bay and the wool twists into fine <part>thread</part>. The crew get dizzy, but the hold fills up with spools. It's a ship built for <kanji>spinning</kanji>.
紡.on: It only stops when it bumps into a <sound>bou</sound>lder sticking out of the water.
紡.kun: The dizzy captain sneezes, '<sound>Tsu</sound>!', and a <sound>moo</sound>se swimming past catches his hat.

宜.meaning: A neighbour leaves a cake on your <part>roof</part>, and <part>moreover</part> a pie on the cake, a jam jar on the pie and a melon on the jar, wobbling up into the clouds. Tucked under the melon is a little card that ends with <kanji>best regards</kanji>.
宜.on: You lower the whole tower by cranking a squeaky <sound>gear</sound> on the chimney.
宜.kun: To say thanks, you send back a <sound>yo</sound>-yo strapped to a toy <sound>ro</sound>cket.

礎.meaning: Before the forest folk build their town hall in the <part>grove</part>, a <part>giant boot</part> stomps one square <part>stone</part> deep into the mud at the first corner. Walls, roof and bell tower all line up from that single block: the <kanji>cornerstone</kanji>.
礎.on: The mayor sits on it like a <sound>so</sound>fa while the walls go up.
礎.kun: Under it they bury a time capsule: a toy <sound>ee</sound>l, a <sound>shee</sound>p's bell, a yu<sound>zu</sound> and an <sound>e</sound>gg.

啓.meaning: A shy spy hides behind a <part>door</part>, cooling herself with a paper <part>fan</part>. A sneeze bangs the door open, the fan flies off, and her <part>mouth</part> blurts out every secret code she knows. Spies must never sneeze: it makes them <kanji>disclose</kanji> everything.
啓.on: Her boss buys her silence with a slice of <sound>ca</sound>ke.
啓.kun: He slams the door so hard that a <sound>hee</sound>l snaps off his shoe and lands in his <sound>ra</sound>men.

桜.meaning: A <part>woman</part> sets off pink <part>fireworks</part> under a bare <part>tree</part> one spring night. Instead of fading, every spark sticks to a twig and turns into a soft pink petal. By morning the whole town has come to picnic under her <kanji>cherry</kanji> tree.
桜.on: Next year she tries it on an <sound>oa</sound>k, which only coughs out acorns.
桜.kun: At the picnic a <sound>sa</sound>rdine slides off a plate, a <sound>coo</sound>k chases it, and a petal lands in his <sound>ra</sound>men.

濁.meaning: A cricket that can only whisper 'sss' falls into a muddy pond. A fisherman scoops it out with his <part>net</part>, shakes off the <part>water drops</part> and gives the <part>insect</part> a warm <part>wrap</part> in his scarf. Now it hums 'zzz' from deep in its throat: the mud made it <kanji>voiced</kanji>.
濁.on: A <sound>du</sound>ck paddles over and trades it a soggy <sound>coo</sound>kie for one more 'zzz'.
濁.kun: The fisherman pulls on his <sound>knee</sound> boots and his <sound>go</sound>ggles, but the pond is too murky to see a thing: to turn muddy.

挿.meaning: Moored by her <part>anchor</part> beside a giant paper <part>sun</part>, a lamplighter pushes a <part>thousand</part> birthday candles into it, one through each tiny hole, until it glows like noon. All night her only job is to <kanji>insert</kanji>.
挿.on: When one won't fit, she rubs it on a bar of <sound>soa</sound>p and it slides right in.
挿.kun: For a joke, she pokes in a <sound>sa</sound>rdine on a stick.

郭.meaning: A ring of walls, with a <part>pennant</part> fluttering on every post, keeps the forest wolves out. Inside, the hens <part>enjoy</part> a picnic, a disco and a hot tub. The wolves peer over the top and sulk: they'd pay to get into that <kanji>enclosure</kanji>.
郭.on: All they get outside is an old fish <sound>carc</sound>ass.
郭.kun: The hens' <sound>coo</sound>k, a <sound>roo</sound>k in an apron, serves them sushi with <sound>wa</sound>sabi.

襟.meaning: A fancy hotel posts a <part>ban</part>: no guests with bare necks. The <part>weathervane</part> from the roof wants the soup of the day, so it spins in the wind until a paper napkin wraps its pole, stiff and starched. The doorman lets it in: nice <kanji>collar</kanji>.
襟.on: At the next table a <sound>kin</sound>gfisher dives straight into its soup.
襟.kun: It dabs the napkin clean with an <sound>e</sound>gg-shaped sponge and a sprig of <sound>ree</sound>d.

蔑.meaning: A <part>sentry</part> guards the palace lawn. A boy runs across the <part>grass</part> swinging a butterfly <part>net</part>, waving, shouting, doing cartwheels. The sentry's eyes never move: his whole job is to <kanji>ignore</kanji> him.
蔑.on: The other guards make <sound>bets</sound> on how long he'll last.
蔑.kun: The boy tries bribes: a <sound>sa</sound>rdine, a pet <sound>ge</sound>cko, a roll of <sound>su</sound>shi. The sentry looks down his nose at all of them.

裸.meaning: A farmer hangs a banana on the <part>weathervane</part> to see which way the wind blows. A cheeky gust peels it in one spin, the skin flying off across three farms. The <part>fruit</part> twirls on top of the barn, totally <kanji>naked</kanji>.
裸.on: The crows on the barn roof flap their wings and cheer, '<sound>Rah</sound>-rah!'
裸.kun: Its peel lands on a <sound>hu</sound>t, bounces off a <sound>du</sound>ck and flops into a <sound>cu</sound>p of tea.

忌.meaning: A <part>cobra</part> curls round a wreath shaped like a <part>heart</part>, wearing a tiny black veil, and sways slowly for its old friend the flute player. For a whole year it won't dance to any tune. Even snakes keep <kanji>mourning</kanji>.
忌.on: It locks the flute in a box and swallows the <sound>key</sound>.
忌.kun: Anyone who tries to play another flute near it gets a hiss and shrieks '<sound>Ee</sound>k!'

蚊.meaning: Every night by your ear, a tiny <part>insect</part> <part>dancer</part> performs her solo, whining one high note as she spins. You clap and clap, but she bows, dodges, and leaves a red itchy bump as her autograph. The star of summer: the <kanji>mosquito</kanji>.
蚊.on: Her biggest fan is a ba<sound>boon</sound>, who scratches his bumps all night.
蚊.kun: You trap her under a <sound>cu</sound>p, but she slips out for an encore.

睡.meaning: A night watchman paints an open <part>eye</part> on each eyelid so his boss thinks he's alert. But his head starts to <part>droop</part>, lower and lower, until the painted eyes stare at his own boots. The boss tiptoes past: he's very <kanji>drowsy</kanji>.
睡.on: Someone tucks a wrapped <sound>swee</sound>t into his top pocket.
睡.kun: He dreams he's waving a butterfly <sound>ne</sound>t, chasing a flying <sound>moo</sound>se.

爽.meaning: A <part>large</part> scarecrow stands in a hot field, arms spread wide, with a wooden <part>lattice</part> strapped under each arm. Every breeze whistles through the gaps, flapping his straw and cooling the crows on his shoulders. Bees queue to sit there: it's so <kanji>refreshing</kanji>.
爽.on: On Sundays the farmer scrubs him with a bar of mint <sound>soa</sound>p.
爽.kun: A crow up there snacks on a <sound>sa</sound>rdine dabbed with <sound>wa</sound>sabi.

闇.meaning: The <part>gate</part> at the edge of town has a <part>chime</part> hanging from its bar. Each time the wind rings it, one lamp in town blinks out, then one star, then the moon. By the hundredth ding nobody can see their own hands: it has begun to <kanji>get dark</kanji>.
闇.on: Your <sound>un</sound>cle stumbles home holding up one birthday candle.
闇.kun: From the pitch black a voice calls, '<sound>Ya</sound>hoo, it's <sound>me</sound>!', and he drops the candle.

煩.meaning: Someone sets a scented candle on the edge of the bath, right next to a <part>rubber duck</part>. The little <part>fire</part> flickers closer every time the water ripples. The duck can't relax: is my tail going soft? Am I melting? Pure <kanji>anxiety</kanji>.
煩.on: To calm its nerves it sips warm <sound>hon</sound>ey tea.
煩.kun: '<sound>Wah</sound>!' squeaks the duck as a yu<sound>zu</sound> rolls into the bath and splashes its <sound>ra</sound>men.

据.meaning: A family wants to <part>reside</part> on a houseboat, but it drifts off every night. So Grandma drops a huge <part>anchor</part>, parks the piano on top of it and plants her rocking chair in the middle of the deck. Nothing moves now: everything is <kanji>set</kanji>.
据.on: Her neighbour opens a tiny floating <sound>kio</sound>sk that sells tea.
据.kun: Grandma sets a plate of <sound>su</sound>shi on the piano lid.

漠.meaning: A painter finishes a perfect <part>sunset</part> on a sea cliff, then rain spatters <part>water drops</part> all over the canvas. Sun, grass and sea run into one soft orange smudge. Buyers squint and guess: a fox? a teapot? It's all very <kanji>vague</kanji>.
漠.on: A cowboy buys it anyway, paying with his shiny belt <sound>buc</sound>kle.

滝.meaning: A <part>dragon</part> squeezes into a mountain lake for a bath. The water spills over the cliff edge, and the <part>water drops</part> become a roaring curtain falling into the valley. Every time it scrubs its back, the <kanji>waterfall</kanji> doubles.
滝.on: It drops in a <sound>ro</sound>se bath bomb, and the whole cliff turns pink.
滝.kun: Down below, hikers eat a <sound>ta</sound>co and a <sound>ki</sound>wi in the pink spray.

尉.meaning: Under the prison <part>flag</part>, a bored guard sets up mini golf in the yard: an old stone <part>altar</part> as a ramp, a mop for a <part>golf club</part>. Prisoners fetch his stray golf balls, and whoever sinks a putt gets extra pudding. He's the jolliest <kanji>jailer</kanji> around.
尉.on: One prisoner keeps a pet <sound>ee</sound>l hidden in the hole.

塞.meaning: A badger's den has a hole in its <part>roof</part>. She lays <part>one</part> plank across it, then <part>eight</part> pebbles, then a big mound of <part>soil</part> on top, patting it flat with her paws. The rain can't get in now: she's managed to <kanji>close</kanji> it.
塞.on: The last little gap she stuffs with an old striped <sound>sock</sound>.
塞.kun: Then she drags her <sound>fu</sound>ton under the patch and lies there munching a <sound>sa</sound>rdine.

拳.meaning: A goat with curly <part>horns</part> rams the gardener's shed every morning. Today the gardener waits with <part>one</part> <part>large</part> <part>hand</part> in an oven glove, curled up tight. Bonk: horns meet glove, and both of them just laugh. An oven glove makes a soft <kanji>fist</kanji>.
拳.on: The goat goes off to sulk in the dog's <sound>ken</sound>nel.
拳.kun: A <sound>co</sound>ckatoo on the fence cheers, waving a <sound>boo</sound>k of boxing tips at a <sound>shee</sound>p.

憧.meaning: A <part>juvenile</part> penguin stands at the zoo fence every afternoon, watching the seagulls swoop. Each time one soars past, its <part>heartbeat</part> skips and it flaps its stubby wings. It doesn't want fish or friends, only sky: all it can do is <kanji>yearn after</kanji> them.
憧.on: Tonight it watches an air <sound>show</sound>, beak pressed to the bars.
憧.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>!' it sighs, as a <sound>co</sound>ckatoo zooms past leading a <sound>ga</sound>ggle of geese.
